chapter: Players and bands of old New Orleans
title: Best trombonists and drummers of the old days
summary: Laurent mentions Lowey Warner, Emanuel Ridgely, Zue Robertson and Vic Gaspar, and praises drummer Cantrell.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: One other question. Who were the best trombone players you remember when you were starting in music? The real all-limers.

Well, I can't think of this fella's name. Used to play with the Imperial Brass Band. He was a good trombone player. Lowey Warner was a good trombone. He had... This fella, he was alright too, but he didn't... He was a good improviser. He didn't read no music or... I see how they call him. He was a great big fella man. He was good too.
Ridgely. Emanuel Ridgely. Emanuel Ridgely. Emanuel Ridgely.
Yeah, he was good too. Do you remember a fella by the name of Zoo Robertson?
Yeah, Zoo Robertson. And, uh... But I didn't know anything of it. But I heard of him. Yeah.
And, uh... How did Oak...not Oak...Vick Gaspar. Was he a good one? Vic Gaspar. Was he a good one?
He was good. Vic was good. He was out at Tranchines with them for 35 years. Was there all that time too. And Cantrell was just as good as a drummer.
Time keepers you could lay your eyes on.
